**Surface verdict: NOT comparable.** Derived from `commands.log` (19 entries), which matches the run's self-reported `tools_called` exactly: stakeout 5, ToolSearch 3, the_receipts 3, collateral_damage 2, shakedown 2, roll_call/blueprint/rap_sheet/manhunt 1 each. The arm stayed inside its declared MCP surface — no filesystem or shell tool — and did call its retriever's search tools. The single disqualifying reason is caching: `cache_read=1265219`, `cache_creation=117403` (the run was warm), so the $2.17 cost is not comparable with cold runs in the series. The scorer's own `not_comparable` list was empty; I recorded that alongside mine in `result.json`.

**What the misses share**: all five sit one layer below the handlers the run actually walked. Three are shared declaration surfaces — `workflows/lib/types.ts`, `prisma/zod-utils.ts`, and the tasker payload entry `sendWorkflowEmails.ts` — schema and type definitions that carry no behaviour of their own and read as plumbing rather than as branding or workflow logic; the other two are the API-v2 versioned booking layer (`bookings.controller.ts`, `input.service.ts`), a parallel entry path into the same booking service the run did retrieve at rank 9. The three hits are all in the workflow-email execution register the answer concentrated on; everything missed is either the type/validation substrate beneath that register or the second, versioned front door into it.
